author: Amr
subject: fix(ci): Playwright 1.58 attachment names, docs front matter, test race (#497)
body:
* fix(ci): match Playwright 1.58+ screenshot attachment names

Playwright 1.58 started naming snapshot attachments with their file
extension ("homepage-air-expected.png") instead of the bare role
("homepage-air-expected"). parse_playwright_results() and
collectFailures() matched suffixes on the raw name, so every image
path resolved to null and the visual-evidence-reviewer brief listed
"expected None / actual None / diff None" for every skin — the
reviewer could never see what changed. Strip a trailing .png/.jpg/
.jpeg before matching the suffix in both implementations.

Also fixes docs/development/extension-points.md (added in #492),
which had no front matter and failed the "Front matter compliance"
check on every PR touching docs/.

Found while reviewing CI failures on #495.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01V8tf4XjvVTaCL1RN5NzFpK

* test(visual): seed cookie consent before the Back to Top click

The ZER0-029 spec scrolled to the bottom of a docs page and clicked
#backToTopBtn without dismissing the cookie banner. On a fresh visit the
banner slides up 1s after DOMContentLoaded, full-width at bottom: 0 on a
layer above the FABs (--zer0-layer-cookie-banner 1095 >
--zer0-layer-fab-back-to-top 1050), so the click passed only when the
load-scroll-click sequence beat that timer. Slow CI runners lost the
race; locally a 1.5s pause before the click reproduces CI's exact
"cookieConsent intercepts pointer events"…

author: Amr
subject: feat(navigation): two clean navbar label tiers, merged chevron, centred grid (#495)
body:
* feat(navigation): two clean navbar label tiers, merged chevron, centred grid

Closes #405.

Collapses the navbar's label density from three container-query tiers to
two: icon + full label above 51rem of centre track, icon-only below it.
Deletes the old bare-label middle tier and its `text-overflow: ellipsis`
safety net — a nav label is now always whole or replaced by its icon,
never clipped to "Quicksta…".

Also, as part of the same coupled change (all five resolve through the
same `bd-nav` container, per the issue's own analysis):
- merges each dropdown's separate chevron button into the parent link's
  hover row (absolutely positioned over reserved padding), closing the
  dead zone between label and chevron while keeping it a real <button>
  with its ARIA intact
- gives the desktop grid's brand/utility side tracks a shared minimum
  width (--zer0-navbar-side-min) so the menubar sits optically centred
  in the bar, without breaking the `1fr` track the container queries
  depend on (the `1fr auto 1fr` spelling the issue suggested collapses
  bd-nav to a degenerate width and silently disables every tier)
- moves the site subtitle out of the navbar (where it competed with nav
  labels for width) onto the home hero instead
- labels the mobile menu toggle "Menu" so it reads differently from the
  sidebar hamburger beside it, with aria-label mirroring the visible
  text so the accessible name satisfies WCAG 2.5.3 in every locale

subject: fix(article): eager-load the hero LCP image and reserve its box (#498)
body:
The article hero (figure.featured-hero) is the above-the-fold LCP element
but inherited preview-image.html's loading="lazy" default and had no
reserved box, so the article jumped by the image height when it landed.

- preview-image.html: optional fetchpriority/decoding params, emitted only
  when passed (every other consumer renders byte-identically).

  decoding="async"; related-post cards keep the lazy default.
- _ui-enhancements.scss: .featured-hero img { aspect-ratio: 3 / 2 } pins
  the box in CSS rather than width/height attributes, since preview
  assets vary in shape (1024x683 generated, portraits, external URLs);
  the existing object-fit: cover crops instead of distorting.
- layouts.spec.js: three smoke tests (attributes, box reserved while the
  image is held, portrait asset) that fail on main and pass here.
- Evidence: test/visual/evidence/hero-lcp/ (476px -> 0px shift).

Closes #485

author: Amr
subject: fix(tests): make the Liquid nested-tag and gem-content checks able to fail (#478)
body:
* fix(tests): make the Liquid nested-tag and gem-content checks able to fail

Both checks in test_core.sh were inert, and one was noisy about it.

test_liquid_templates grepped for `{{.*{{`, which matches any two SIBLING
output tags on one line: 64 of the theme's includes matched, starting with
navigation/sidebar-pagetree.html's valid `{{ _base }}{{ _section }}` inside
a capture. Its `return 1` then sat inside a `find | while` pipeline -- a
subshell -- so the function printed "[ERROR] Nested Liquid output tags found
in ..." on every clean run and still returned 0. The pattern is now
`{{[^}]*{{`, which cannot cross the first `}`, and both loops read from a
process substitution so a match actually fails the suite.

test_gem_build ran `tar -tzf` on the built .gem. A gem is an UNCOMPRESSED
tar wrapping metadata.gz, data.tar.gz and checksums.yaml.gz, so gzip printed
"stdin: not in gzip format" four times and both branches fell through to
"Gem may not contain ..." warnings without inspecting anything -- a gem with
no _layouts/ at all would have passed. The assertions move into
check_gem_contents(), which extracts data.tar.gz, lists it, and requires
both _layouts/ and assets/ as directories rather than as substrings.

test/test_core_checks.sh is new: it sources test_core.sh (whose `main` call
is now guarded on BASH_SOURCE == $0) and drives both checks against
known-good and known-bad fixtures, including .gem fixtures built to the real
RubyGems layout. A check that stops being able t…

author: Amr
subject: ci(visual-evidence): stop label events from starting cancelled runs (#480)
body:
* ci(visual-evidence): stop label events from starting cancelled runs

`visual-evidence-autogen` triggers on `labeled`, but a label event can
only ever suppress this lane — never create work for it. Each one still
started a run, and the per-PR concurrency group (`cancel-in-progress:
true`, already correct) then killed whatever render was in flight.

PR #478 is the whole failure in one PR: opened 09:05:09Z, five labels
applied at 09:05:10Z (`bug`, `area:tests`, `risk:low`, `skip-evidence`,
`automation`), six runs fired, five ended `cancelled`. Four of those
labels mean nothing to this workflow. Over the last 14 days: 19
`cancelled` and 7 `skipped` runs out of 82.

Drop `labeled` from the trigger types. Keep `unlabeled` — removing
`skip-evidence` / `no-visual-change` is the one label change that
legitimately re-enables a run — and narrow it in the job `if:` to
exactly those two labels, so removing an unrelated label no longer
starts a run either.

author: Amr
subject: fix(includes): stop the draft chip shifting the Site Builder on first save (#489)
body:
* fix(includes): stop the draft chip shifting the Site Builder on first save

showDraftChip() cleared the "Draft saved" chip's `hidden` attribute, and the 2s
timer that follows only removes `is-visible` — an opacity class. So the first
debounced save moved the chip from `display: none` into layout permanently. Its
box is 26px against the 19px "Start over" .btn-sm beside it, so .wizard-header
grew and stayed grown, taking #wizardTabContent and every Back/Next row below
it down with it.

That is the `@critical` failure on every push to main:

  Next button document-y offsets across steps: 2029, 2036, 2036, 2036, 2036,
  2036, 2036, 2036

Connect was not 7px off. Connect was the step measured before the 300ms save
debounce fired; every step after it was measured after. Deterministic rather
than flaky, because a one-way state transition is deterministic — which is also
why the identical byte sequence appeared in two independent runs and the retry.

_setup-wizard.scss already described the intended behaviour in prose ("Kept in
the layout (no display toggling) so its appearance never shifts the header").
It was only ever prose: the markup carried `hidden` and the JS cleared it. The
chip now holds its box from first paint and is hidden with `visibility`, which
makes the comment true and still keeps the chip out of the accessibility tree
while it has nothing to say.

Measured on a live wizard at 1280px, cold and then after one keystroke:

  before   header 107 -> 149 px, #wizardTabCo…

subject: chore(dev): adopt the fleet .vscode run/debug convention (fleet-vscode/v1) (#479)
body:
One layout for every repo in the workspace: tasks.json RUNS (Serve / Stop /
Build / Verify / Lint / Test / Claude: session + repo extras), launch.json
DEBUGS (Edge on top of Serve, the live site, node/python/extension-host
debuggers), settings.json holds repo-scoped settings only, extensions.json the
fleet core set + this stack. Every task delegates to the script CI runs;
`docker compose` (v2) everywhere; the convention is written down in
.vscode/README.md, byte-identical across the repos.

This repo: collapses the per-tier / per-project / per-bump task copies into pickString inputs (30 → 19 tasks, same coverage), drops the pinned userDataDir profiles and the attach / mobile / perf / rebuild launch variants (DevTools device toolbar covers mobile; Docker: rebuild is a task) and the standalone :4011 Playwright path; docs/systems/gem-publication-system.md now lists the real task names.

author: Amr
subject: fix(ci): keep a LiveReload push from crashing the generic evidence generator (#500)
body:
pr-evidence.mjs died at its third width on #495 (run 36932006025) with
"page.$: Execution context was destroyed" and wrote no metrics or PNGs,
while the job still went green.

Root cause: the autogen lane serves the PR head with
`jekyll serve --watch --livereload`. jekyll-watch ignores only the
`exclude:` paths that exist when its watcher starts, and on a fresh CI
checkout node_modules/ does not. The jammy container's `npm ci` then
writes ~4,600 files into it, Jekyll regenerates (two waves, ~8-12s each),
and LiveReload reloads every open page. The reload landed between the
overflow measurement and the header lookup. "Third width" is only timing.

- pr-evidence.mjs: abort the injected livereload.js (the static BEFORE
  site never had it, and the served HTML does not change, so there is
  nothing to wait for), and guard the remaining page-context calls
  (overflow evaluate, header lookup) so one width can never abort the
  sweep.
- visual_evidence_autogen.py: create node_modules/ before
  `docker compose up` so the watcher ignores it and `npm ci` no longer
  regenerates the site under the generator or the snapshot verify pass.
- test_visual_evidence_autogen.py: pin both ends; all three new checks
  fail against main.

body:
auto-merge.yml's guard ran `gh pr edit --remove-label` with no checkout and
no GH_REPO, so gh died with 'not a git repository' and the label stayed. And
dependabot-auto-merge.yml labelled github_actions bumps, which always touch

The lane pushes its evidence commit with a PAT, which fires synchronize;
the workflow-level concurrency group then cancelled the run that pushed,
recording 7-16 billed minutes as cancelled each time. A cheap guard job
now skips autogen when the head subject carries [visual-autogen], and the
concurrency group moves to the autogen job so a skipped run never joins it.

author: Amr
subject: fix(tests): serve the Visual Snapshots stack without LiveReload (#530)
body:
* fix(tests): serve the Visual Snapshots stack without LiveReload

The snapshots tier retried appearance-snapshot.spec.js on most CI runs with
"Execution context was destroyed, most likely because of a navigation".
docker compose up starts `jekyll serve --watch --livereload` over a bind
mount, and update-snapshots.sh then runs `npm ci` into that mount; on a fresh
checkout node_modules/ is not yet ignored by the watcher, so the install
regenerates the site and LiveReload reloads the page mid-test.

- docker-compose.yml: JEKYLL_LIVERELOAD=0 drops --livereload and layers
  _config_snapshots.yml (livereload: false). The overlay is needed because
  _config_dev.yml sets `livereload: true`, so dropping the flag alone left
  LiveReload on.
- update-snapshots.sh starts the stack with JEKYLL_LIVERELOAD=0, records the
  root cause in its header, and fails before Playwright (in CI, or when it
  started the stack) if test/lib/assert_no_livereload.sh finds LiveReload
  still live.

Default `docker compose up` is unchanged (LiveReload on).

* docs(changelog): note the snapshot-stack LiveReload fix (#461)

* chore(backlog): mark T-050 done (#461)

* fix(validate): classify _config_snapshots.yml in the config contract

---------

Co-authored-by: bamr87 <bamr87@users.noreply.github.com>

author: Amr
subject: fix(analytics): load GA and PostHog only after analytics consent (#539)
body:
* fix(analytics): load GA and PostHog only after analytics consent

With posthog.privacy.require_consent: true, PostHog still fetched array.js,
config.js and surveys.js and set its ph_* cookie before the visitor chose
anything in the cookie banner, and Google Analytics ignored consent.

PostHog's loader and init now run in a one-shot boot that fires at parse
time only when consent exists, otherwise on the banner's
cookieConsentChanged event. The GA include follows the same flag
(google_analytics_require_consent overrides it) and loads on the same
event, so accepting takes effect without a reload. Reject keeps both off.
Sites without the flag are unchanged.

* test(analytics): compare the routed origin exactly (CodeQL js/incomplete-url-substring-sanitization)

* test(visual): before/after evidence for this PR (generated locally with test/visual/pr-evidence.mjs; CI autogen stack is failing its LiveReload check)

author: Amr
subject: feat(studio): zer0 studio — the Rails workbench beside the theme (#560)
body:
* feat(studio): zer0 studio — the Rails workbench beside the theme

A Rails 8.1 app at studio/ that designs, customizes and updates this theme
from a browser, against the files in the checkout, with the theme's own
scripts doing the work.

Design: each _sass/tokens/* file with its _design-system/tokens/* mirror,
edited together by byte-range splice (ScssDeclarations) so comments and
formatting survive; a skin's palette across _skins.scss, skins.css,
_backgrounds.scss and theme_backgrounds.yml with the RGB triplet derived
from the brand; a live unified diff under every form; WCAG 2.1 contrast per
skin; scripts/design-system-check.rb after every save. A read-only doctor
(token parity, the skin registries, background assets the gem does not
ship, link contrast, the settings page's byte copy, the studio/ exclusion)
with findings.jsonl-shaped output. Docs-site previews built as jobs with
bundle exec jekyll build and shown from the other loopback origin.

Customize: consumer checkouts under SITES_DIR registered by realpath, their
theme keys in _config.yml rewritten one line at a time, audit-consumer as a
job whose JSON report lands on the site, consumers.yml joined by name.

Update: the six version files against version.rb, release --dry-run and
propagate.rb in report mode as jobs. Nothing here releases or dispatches.

Every write is a digest-guarded atomic rename (409 when stale) of a file an
allow-list names, every path goes through ConfinedPath, every process
through ScriptRunne…

body:
* refactor(theme): ship no person in the shared includes and layout

components/author-eeat.html defaulted its author to a hard-coded key; it now takes
site.author.key, then the default entry of _data/authors.yml, then its first entry.
content/jsonld-software.html emitted a fixed Person; it now builds one from site.founder,
site.author.name or site.title and the site's github_user. The root layout no longer carries
a personal copyright comment. The theme's docs site and sites/zer0-pages keep their byline by
setting author.key in their own _config.yml, which is where a site's identity belongs.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Ported-From: bamr87/zer0-CMS@eae58c3e
Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(zer0-mistakes): assign the latest-posts limit before the for loop

The installer's landing-page template (genIndex in
assets/js/setup-wizard.js) and the two demo sites generated from it
render a latest_posts section with

  {% for post in site.posts limit: s.limit | default: 3 %}

Liquid accepts no filter inside a for tag's limit: clause. Jekyll logs
"Liquid Warning: Liquid syntax error (line 38): Expected end_of_string
but found pipe", drops the whole capture block from the page and exits

author: Amr
subject: ci: stop the two recurring red/cancelled run sources on main
body:
Over the five weeks to 2026-10-29 `main` decided 197 runs and only 2
actually failed; the headline pass rate was dragged down by 37 cancelled
and 166 skipped runs. Two of those sources are fixable in-repo.

1. Dependabot errored on every re-check of the rubyzip advisory
   (2026-09-26, 10-03, 10-07, 10-27). The fix needs >= 3.4.0, but
   github-pages (232) requires rubyzip (>= 1.3.0, < 3.0) through
   jekyll-remote-theme (0.4.3), so security_update_not_possible failed
   the whole update run. Add a bundler entry whose only job is to ignore
   rubyzip >= 3.0 — version updates stay off, so update-dependencies.yml
   keeps ownership of gems, and security updates are unaffected by that
   limit. The advisory stays visible in the Security tab; remove the
   entry when github-pages allows rubyzip 3.x.

2. issue-autopilot used a workflow-level concurrency group with a
   constant name, so every `issues: [labeled]` event joined it even
   though gate's job-level `if` skips them all. With one pass running
   and one queued, each further no-op label event cancelled the queued
   run: 13 of the 37 cancellations. Non-actionable label events now get
   their own group; real passes (schedule, dispatch, autopilot:go) stay
   serialized under the shared name.

Co-authored-by: bamr87 <bamr87@users.noreply.github.com>
Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
